learn.hook: A boy who grew up among the hills of the Sahyadris went on to build a kingdom from a handful of forts. His name was Shivaji.
points: Shivaji was born in 1630 at Shivneri fort near Pune. His father was Shahaji Bhonsle and his mother was Jijabai, who shaped his values and courage.
He began by capturing hill forts in the Sahyadris (Western Ghats) and built up swarajya, his own self-rule.
In 1659 he defeated Afzal Khan, a general of the Bijapur Sultanate, at Pratapgad. In 1666 he made a famous escape from Aurangzeb's custody in Agra.
His soldiers used guerrilla warfare: small, fast groups that knew the hills well and struck by surprise.
In 1674 he was crowned at Raigad fort and took the title Chhatrapati. He died in 1680.

example.q: Think it through: Why did guerrilla warfare suit the Marathas in the Sahyadri hills?
steps: The Sahyadris have steep slopes, narrow passes and thick forests.
Large armies with heavy guns and elephants move slowly there.
Small Maratha bands knew every path and could attack quickly and vanish.
Hill forts gave them safe bases to rest and store supplies.
example.answer: The rough hills slowed big armies, while small, fast Maratha groups who knew the land could strike and retreat to their forts.

learn.reallife: Shivneri, Raigad and Pratapgad still stand in Maharashtra, and many school trips climb these forts every year.

games.title: True or false?
items: Shivaji was born at Shivneri fort.
Shivneri, near Junnar in Pune district, is his birthplace.
Shivaji was crowned at Raigad in 1674.
He took the title Chhatrapati at his coronation there.
His mother was Jijabai. Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi lived in the 19th century.
Guerrilla warfare relies on huge, slow-moving armies.
It uses small, quick groups that attack by surprise.
Afzal Khan was a general of the Bijapur Sultanate.
Bijapur sent him against Shivaji in 1659.

quiz.q: Where was Shivaji born?
quiz.explain: Shivaji was born at Shivneri in 1630.
quiz.mistake: Confuses his birthplace with his capital

quiz.q: Who was Shivaji's mother?
quiz.explain: Jijabai raised Shivaji and inspired him.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up famous Maratha women

quiz.q: In which year was Shivaji crowned Chhatrapati?
quiz.explain: His coronation took place at Raigad in 1674.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the dates of his life

quiz.q: What kind of fighting did Shivaji's soldiers use in the hills?
quiz.explain: Small groups made surprise attacks using their knowledge of the terrain.
quiz.mistake: Picks a style of war from another time or place

quiz.q: Which general of Bijapur did Shivaji defeat at Pratapgad in 1659?
quiz.explain: Shivaji defeated Afzal Khan at Pratapgad.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the generals Shivaji faced

quiz.q: From whose custody in Agra did Shivaji escape in 1666?
quiz.explain: Shivaji was held at Aurangzeb's court in Agra and escaped.
quiz.mistake: Picks a Mughal emperor from the wrong time

quiz.q: The Sahyadris, where Shivaji built his forts, are also called:
quiz.explain: The Sahyadri range is the Western Ghats.
quiz.mistake: Confuses Indian mountain ranges

quiz.q: Shivaji was born in 1630 and crowned in 1674. How old was he at his coronation (about)?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts carelessly

teach.ask: Gappu has heard the name Shivaji but knows nothing more. Tell Gappu the key events of Shivaji's life.
teach.praise: From Shivneri to Raigad, what a journey! I want to climb those forts.
teach.nudge: Where was he born? How did he fight, and when was he crowned?

learn.hook: A king cannot run a kingdom alone. Shivaji had a team of eight ministers, a navy and a ring of strong forts.
points: Shivaji was helped by a council of eight ministers called the Ashtapradhan. The Peshwa was the chief minister.
Forts were the backbone of his kingdom. He built and repaired many, including sea forts like Sindhudurg on the Konkan coast.
He built a navy to protect the coast and trade from foreign powers such as the Portuguese and the Siddis of Janjira.
He collected chauth, one-fourth (25%) of the revenue, and sardeshmukhi, an extra one-tenth (10%), from areas outside his direct rule.
He paid many soldiers and officials in cash instead of giving them land, so that they stayed loyal to the state.

example.q: Think it through: A district's land revenue is ₹1,000. If the Marathas collected chauth from it, how much would that be?
steps: Chauth means one-fourth of the revenue.

learn.reallife: Sindhudurg sea fort near Malvan was built on an island; boats still carry visitors there. The Indian Navy honours Shivaji's naval vision.

games.title: Match the term
pairs: Sea fort on the Konkan coast

items.q: How many ministers were in the Ashtapradhan?

quiz.q: What was the Ashtapradhan?
quiz.explain: Ashta means eight; pradhan means minister.
quiz.mistake: Guesses the meaning without knowing the term

quiz.q: Who was the chief minister in the Ashtapradhan?
quiz.explain: The Peshwa was the chief minister; the Senapati was the army chief.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the army chief with the chief minister

quiz.q: Chauth was a tax equal to what share of the revenue?
quiz.explain: Chauth comes from the word for 'fourth'.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up chauth and sardeshmukhi

quiz.q: Sardeshmukhi was an extra tax of:
quiz.explain: Sardeshmukhi was an additional 10% of the revenue.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up chauth and sardeshmukhi

quiz.q: Why did Shivaji build a navy?
options: To travel to Delhi by river
To protect the coast and sea trade
quiz.explain: The Konkan coast faced threats from foreign and coastal powers.
quiz.mistake: Does not link the navy with coastal defence

quiz.q: Sindhudurg is an example of:
quiz.explain: It was built on an island off the Konkan coast.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all Maratha forts were in the hills

quiz.q: Why did Shivaji prefer paying many soldiers in cash rather than land?
options: Because soldiers did not want salaries
So they stayed loyal to the state, not to their own estates
quiz.explain: Land grants could make officers independent; cash pay kept them dependent on the state.
quiz.mistake: Misses the political reason behind the pay system

quiz.q: A region's revenue is ₹2,000. What is the chauth on it?
quiz.explain: Chauth = one-fourth: 2000 ÷ 4 = 500.
quiz.mistake: Uses one-tenth instead of one-fourth

teach.ask: Gappu wants to be a good king. Explain to Gappu how Shivaji ran his kingdom.
teach.praise: Eight ministers, a navy and strong forts! Gappu's kingdom will be well run.
teach.nudge: Who helped Shivaji govern? How did he protect his kingdom and collect money?

learn.hook: From the hills of Maharashtra, Maratha horsemen rode as far as Delhi, Odisha and the Punjab within a hundred years of Shivaji.
points: After Shivaji, his sons Sambhaji and Rajaram, and later Rajaram's widow Tarabai, kept fighting the Mughals in the Deccan.
In the 18th century, the Peshwas became the real leaders of the Maratha state, with Pune as their centre. Bajirao I led campaigns deep into north India.
Maratha chiefs set up their own strong states: the Holkars at Indore, the Scindias (Shindes) at Gwalior, the Gaekwads at Baroda and the Bhonsles at Nagpur.
In 1761 the Marathas lost the Third Battle of Panipat to Ahmad Shah Abdali of Afghanistan, but they soon recovered much of their power.

Ahilyabai Holkar, who ruled from Maheshwar, is remembered for good administration and for building and repairing temples, ghats and wells across India. The Marathas were finally defeated by the British in 1818.

example.q: Think it through: Why is the Maratha state of the 18th century often called a confederacy?
steps: A confederacy is a group of states joined together.
The Peshwa at Pune was the overall leader.
Chiefs like the Holkars, Scindias, Gaekwads and Bhonsles ruled their own regions.
They worked together, though they were quite independent in their own areas.
example.answer: Because several powerful Maratha chiefs ruled their own states while accepting the Peshwa as their head.

learn.reallife: The royal palaces of Gwalior and Baroda and the ghats of Maheshwar on the Narmada are reminders of the Maratha chiefs.

items.text: The Third Battle of Panipat was fought in ___.
The Marathas lost at Panipat to Ahmad Shah ___.
After Rajaram died, his widow ___ led the fight against the Mughals.
Ahilyabai Holkar ruled from ___ on the Narmada.

quiz.q: Who were the real leaders of the Maratha state for most of the 18th century?
quiz.explain: The Peshwas, based in Pune, led the Maratha state.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the Mughals still controlled the Marathas

quiz.q: Which Peshwa led Maratha armies deep into north India in the 1720s and 1730s?
quiz.explain: Bajirao I was famous for his fast cavalry campaigns northwards.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up Peshwas and kings

quiz.q: Against whom did the Marathas fight the Third Battle of Panipat?
quiz.explain: Ahmad Shah Abdali (Durrani) of Afghanistan defeated them in 1761.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the three battles of Panipat

quiz.q: The Scindia family ruled from:
quiz.explain: The Scindias (Shindes) made Gwalior their centre.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the Maratha families

quiz.q: Ahilyabai Holkar is best remembered for:
options: Good administration and building temples, ghats and wells
quiz.explain: She ruled from Maheshwar and is admired for her wise, caring rule.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up historical figures

quiz.q: Which battle did the Marathas lose in 1761?
quiz.explain: The Third Battle of Panipat was fought on 14 January 1761.
quiz.mistake: Confuses battles of the 18th century

quiz.q: Which statement about the Maratha confederacy is correct?
options: It was ruled directly by the Mughal emperor
Several Maratha chiefs ruled their own regions under the Peshwa's leadership
quiz.explain: Holkars, Scindias, Gaekwads and Bhonsles ruled regions while accepting the Peshwa as head.
quiz.mistake: Misunderstands what a confederacy is

quiz.q: Shivaji died in 1680 and the Third Battle of Panipat was in 1761. How many years apart were these?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts carelessly

teach.ask: Gappu thinks the Marathas stopped after Shivaji. Explain how Maratha power spread.
teach.praise: From Pune to Panipat! The Marathas really spread far.
teach.nudge: Who led the Marathas after Shivaji? Which families ruled where, and what happened in 1761?
